subject: Mixed (Real Weightage)
description: 100 questions following the real PGP-CET 2025 subject weightage. Mix: 32 easy / 68 medium / 0 hard. Tier is relative: the easy third of the 60 papers by average question difficulty. Every question cites its source.

questions.question: The recommended total weight gain in a normal pregnancy is about:
questions.explanation: Depends on pre-pregnancy BMI.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: On the dyspnoea scale, a +4 grade is when dyspnoea causes:

options.C: Severe difficulty so the patient cannot continue his activity

questions.explanation: +4 is severe breathlessness that stops the activity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: In grade 3+ pitting oedema:

options.B: The pitting is 1/4-1/2 inch and rebounds in 15 seconds
options.C: The indentation is severe with pitting of 1/2-1 inch that rebounds in about 15-30 seconds
options.D: The pitting is over 1 inch and lasts over 30 seconds

questions.explanation: 3+ is severe oedema with a deeper, slower-rebounding pit.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: In late pregnancy, which position can cause symptomatic supine hypotension?
questions.explanation: The gravid uterus compresses the inferior vena cava in supine, reducing venous return.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: An example of a second-class lever in the human body is:
questions.explanation: In a second-class lever the load lies between the fulcrum and the effort, as in plantar flexion with the ball of the foot as fulcrum.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: In an underwater seal chest drain, the tip of the drainage tube is kept about ______ below the water surface.
questions.explanation: A tip 2-3 cm under water acts as a one-way valve with minimal resistance.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Hip joint is weakest in which of the following attitudes?
questions.explanation: The hip is weakest in flexion, adduction and internal rotation (dislocation position).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Kinesiology of Musculoskeletal System/Neuman/Pg. 400
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: When analgesia is the goal, which of the following ions is NOT used in iontophoresis?
questions.explanation: Zinc is used for dermal ulcers, not analgesia.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The normal age of response of the Landau reflex is:
questions.explanation: The Landau reaction appears at about 4 months and is integrated by 12-24 months.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Skeletal muscles in a normal adult contribute:

options.A: 10 to 15% to the total body weight
options.B: 15 to 20% to the total body weight
options.C: 40 to 50% to the total body weight
options.D: 0 to 5% to the total body weight

questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle forms about 40-50 percent of adult body weight.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Pathological Q waves in leads I and aVL indicate:
questions.explanation: Leads I and aVL view the high lateral wall.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: A patient with a transfemoral amputation begins gait training with prosthesis. What effect will a hip flexion contracture have on the patient's gait?

options.A: The patient will demonstrate increased stability in the prosthetic knee
options.B: The patient's step length on the prosthetic side will be increased.
options.C: The hip flexion contracture will not affect the patient's gait pattern
options.D: The patient will not begin to ambulate until normal range of motion is restored

questions.explanation: A hip flexion contracture shortens the step of the opposite limb and affects prosthetic stability and step length.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Tidy's Physiotherapy/KM Varghese/12th Ed./Pg. 269
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Most common bone fractured during birth:
questions.explanation: The clavicle is the bone most commonly fractured during birth.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: The joint surfaces are maximally congruent and the capsule and ligaments taut in the:
questions.explanation: In the close-packed position, the joint is locked and has no joint play.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Which illness is characterized by bronchial hyper irritability that is triggered by a number of stimuli resulting in narrowing of the air passages?
questions.explanation: Bronchial hyper-irritability with reversible narrowing defines asthma.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: On the original Borg 6-20 RPE scale, 11 corresponds to:
questions.explanation: 11 is fairly light.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: When the p-value is more than the alpha value, the null hypothesis is:
questions.explanation: A non-significant result fails to reject the null hypothesis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: A patient involved in a motor vehicle accident sustains a fracture of the proximal fibula. The fracture damages the motor component of the common peroneal nerve. Exercise Therapy 5 Ankle dorsiflexion and eversion are tested as 2/5. The most appropriate intervention to assist patient with activities of daily living would be:

options.D: An exercise program E. An aquatic program

questions.explanation: Foot drop from common peroneal nerve injury is best managed with an ankle-foot orthosis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: When a convex joint surface moves on a fixed concave surface, the roll and glide occur:
questions.explanation: Convex on concave: gliding is opposite to the rolling direction (e.g. humeral head in abduction).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Helium neon laser has penetration of up to:
questions.explanation: He-Ne laser penetrates up to about 6 mm in this source.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Physical Agent in Rehabilitation/Cameron/2nd Ed./Pg. 383
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The normal inspiratory to expiratory (I:E) ratio at rest is:
questions.explanation: Expiration is normally about twice as long as inspiration.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The Q angle is utilized as a measure to determine the amount of lateral force on the patella. Which three bony landmarks are used to measure the Q angle?

options.A: Anterior superior iliac spine, superior border of the patella, tibial tubercle
options.B: Anterior superior iliac spine, midpoint of the patella, tibial tubercle
options.C: Anterior superior iliac inferior border of the patella, midpoint of the patella tendon
options.D: Greater trochanter midpoint of the patella, superior border of the patella tendon

questions.explanation: Q angle is formed between lines from the ASIS to the midpoint of the patella and from the patella midpoint to the tibial tubercle.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Kinesiology of Musurloskeletal System/Neuman/Pg. 461
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: An adult sustained a fracture of the both bones of mid forearm at the same level. After manipulation the position of immobilisation of the forearm in the plaster would be:
questions.explanation: After manipulation both-bone forearm fractures are immobilised in mid-prone.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A physical therapist observes that a patient's medial longitudinal arch is extremely depressed. Which ligament helps to maintain the medial longtitudnal arch?
questions.explanation: The plantar calcaneonavicular (spring) ligament is a key static support of the medial longitudinal arch.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Joint Structure and Function/Norkin/3rd Ed./Pg. 399
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Most common cause of scoliosis is:
questions.explanation: Idiopathic scoliosis is the commonest type of scoliosis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Trendelenburg's sign is said to be positive when:

options.A: Sound side pelvis drop down while standing on affected side
options.B: Affected side pelvis drop down while standing on sound side
options.C: Sound side pelvis elevated while standing on affected side

questions.explanation: The Trendelenburg sign is positive when the pelvis drops on the sound side while standing on the affected leg.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/Magee/ 5th Ed./Pg. 7
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Practice in which rest time is greater than practice time is:
questions.explanation: Distributed practice includes frequent rest periods.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Which condition is associated with a positive HLA-B27?
questions.explanation: About 90 percent of patients with ankylosing spondylitis are HLA-B27 positive.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Which type of research studies complex human behaviour?
questions.explanation: Qualitative research explores meaning, experience and behaviour.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Menorrhagia is defined as menstrual blood loss of more than:
questions.explanation: Common causes: fibroids, dysfunctional uterine bleeding.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Repetitive practice of the same task is called:
questions.explanation: Blocked practice repeats one task before moving to the next.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Precordial lead V3 is placed:

options.B: 4th intercostal space at the right sternal border
options.C: 5th intercostal space at the mid-clavicular line

questions.explanation: V3 lies between V2 and V4.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Which mode is commonly used to wean a patient from mechanical ventilation?
questions.explanation: Synchronised intermittent mandatory ventilation lets the patient take over breaths progressively.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Which statement best describes the realistic functional status of a patient with C4 tetraplegia after completing rehabilitation?

options.B: Independent in all activities of daily living
options.C: Able to propel a manual wheelchair independently
options.D: Able to operate a power wheelchair

questions.explanation: C4 tetraplegia can operate a power wheelchair.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The characteristic vascular lesion in malignant hypertension is:
questions.explanation: Rapid renal failure and papilloedema.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Skin resistance can be decreased by:
questions.explanation: Warming lowers skin resistance.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The following is true of spondylolisthesis:
questions.explanation: Spondylolisthesis is forward slip of one vertebra (usually L5 on S1) associated with a defect of the pars/posterior arch.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Who is acclaimed worldwide for total joint replacement?
questions.explanation: Sir John Charnley pioneered low-friction total hip replacement.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: The normal fasting blood glucose is:
questions.explanation: Impaired fasting glucose: 100–125 mg/dL.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: Marble bone disease is also known as:
questions.explanation: Marble bone disease is osteopetrosis (Albers-Schonberg disease).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Crazy bone or crazy nerve contusion is associated with:

options.C: Radial nerve at spiral groove in humerus

questions.explanation: Contusion of the ulnar nerve at the elbow is the "funny bone" injury.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: A gomphosis (peg-in-socket fibrous joint) is the joint between:
questions.explanation: Gomphosis is the fibrous attachment of a tooth to its alveolar socket.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Chronaxie is equal to the pulse duration at ______ rheobase.
questions.explanation: Chronaxie is the shortest pulse duration needed to excite tissue at twice the rheobase intensity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Which pain is improving with exercise?
questions.explanation: The pain of ankylosing spondylitis improves with exercise and worsens with rest.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Ulnar nerve entrapment at the wrist occurs in:
questions.explanation: Guyon's canal is formed by the pisiform and hook of hamate.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient with a suspected acutely torn medial meniscus. Which symptom is not commonly associated with a medial meniscus tear?

options.A: Tenderness along the medial point line

questions.explanation: Hamstring atrophy is not a feature of a medial meniscus tear (quadriceps atrophy is).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Which aphasia is fluent but with impaired language comprehension?
questions.explanation: Wernicke's aphasia is fluent with poor comprehension.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The ordinal scale:

options.C: Has equal intervals and a true zero

questions.explanation: Ordinal data have order but unequal intervals (e.g. MMT grades).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Which historical event brought major attention to drug teratogenicity, resulting in thousands of infants born with phocomelia (seal-like limbs)?
questions.explanation: The thalidomide disaster (1958-61) resulted in thousands of babies born with phocomelia and other defects after the drug was used by pregnant women, and is the landmark event that focused medical attention on drug teratogenicity.
questions.sourceBook: KD Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: A therapist is asked to indicate on a five point scale how competent a patient is in a selected transfer technique. The scale ranges from totally incompetent to extremely competent. The type of scale utilizes a/an _______ level of measurement?
questions.explanation: A rating scale from incompetent to competent is ordinal.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methods for Clinical Therapists/Hicks/4th Ed./Pg. 35

questions.question: Amoebic liver abscess is caused by:
questions.explanation: Anchovy sauce pus.

questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminaemia and generalised oedema define:
questions.explanation: Proteinuria above 3.5 g per day with low albumin and oedema.
questions.sourceBook: Original question prepared for this simulator from standard textbook knowledge
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Axons conduct impulses ______ the cell body.
questions.explanation: Dendrites receive signals towards the soma; the axon carries them away.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: On the dyspnoea scale, a +2 grade is when dyspnoea is:

options.B: Moderate with the patient able to continue
options.D: Mild and noticeable to the observer

questions.explanation: +2 means mild difficulty that the observer can see.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Oedema due to hypoalbuminaemia is caused by:
questions.explanation: Seen in nephrotic syndrome, cirrhosis and malnutrition.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: In monopolar technique the dispersive electrode:
questions.explanation: The large dispersive electrode minimises current density.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The alternating vasodilatation and vasoconstriction during the application of cold is:
questions.explanation: Alternating vasoconstriction and vasodilatation in the cold is the Lewis hunting reaction.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The rotator cuff is composed of four of the following muscles except:
questions.explanation: The rotator cuff is supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis; teres major is not part of it.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: A therapist visits a former patient diagnosed with pneumonic plague in the hospital. The patient is in strict isolation, but the therapist has been granted permission to visit if there is no body contact. What protective measures are necessary when entering the room of a patient in strict isolation?
questions.explanation: Strict isolation requires mask, gown and gloves.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: The area responsible for the sensory aspect (comprehension) of speech is:
questions.explanation: Wernicke's area (posterior superior temporal gyrus) handles speech comprehension.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The most common cause of ischaemic stroke is:

options.B: Thromboembolism from atherosclerosis or the heart

questions.explanation: Most strokes are ischaemic and thromboembolic.
questions.sourceBook: Original question prepared for this simulator from standard textbook knowledge
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Ortolani's test is done for:
questions.explanation: Ortolani's test is for congenital dislocation of the hip.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Golfer's elbow (medial epicondylitis) mainly involves:

options.C: Flexor carpi radialis and pronator teres

questions.explanation: The common flexor origin, chiefly FCR and pronator teres, is affected.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: In the Hoehn and Yahr classification, stage 1 Parkinson's disease is:

options.A: Bilateral involvement with balance not affected
options.B: Severe disability needing assistance to walk

questions.explanation: Stage 1: unilateral signs only.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: A Modified Ashworth grade of 1 indicates a slight increase in tone with:

options.C: Resistance through most of the range
options.D: A catch and release or minimal resistance at the end of the range

questions.explanation: MAS 1: slight increase in tone, a catch and release or minimal resistance at the end of ROM.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Ideal site for bone graft harvesting:
questions.explanation: The iliac crest is the usual donor site for cancellous bone graft.

questions.question: Piriformis muscle is inserted at:
questions.explanation: Piriformis inserts into the greater trochanter.

questions.explanation: Milgram studied obedience.

questions.question: The chronic form of filariasis, characterised by lymphoedema and gross thickening of the skin of the legs/scrotum, is known as:

questions.question: A therapist is concerned about the possibility of a patient developing a deep vein thrombosis following surgery. Which of the following special test would be useful to identify the presence of a deep vein thrombosis?

questions.question: SWD is used for all of the following except:

questions.question: According to common guidelines, hypertension is diagnosed when blood pressure is persistently at or above:

questions.question: Lifting a dumbbell through a range is an example of:

questions.question: Precordial lead V4 is placed at the:

questions.question: The switches in the apparatus should break:

questions.question: To facilitate wound healing, protein intake should be maintained at about:

questions.question: A butcher is responsible for processing meat packaging. In the process of carving the meat he injures the second and third digits of his hand. The hand surgeon reports that the nerves in the second and third digits have been permanently injured. Which nerve/nerves would be injured?
questions.explanation: The median nerve supplies sensation to the index and middle fingers (digits 2 and 3) on the palmar side.
